t: You're at the site of the Saracen's Head, a coaching inn and pub that stood on the north side of the street, just west of the church of St Sepulchre-without-Newgate on Snow Hill. It closed in 1868. Sarah Ann Mountain owned it, and she was a coach, mail and inn proprietor. Under her, stagecoaches were made here, and fifteen of them left each day for places including Birmingham and Leeds. She also ran the last coach from Bristol to London.
